speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To understand the cause of your double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness, please describe exactly when these symptoms first started and if they affect one side of your body more than the other.

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those symptoms of worsening weakness with activity and improvement with rest, along with double vision triggered by looking up or down, strongly suggest Myasthenia Gravis. To confirm this, I need to see the results of your acetylcholine receptor antibody test and a single fiber EMG. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_receptor_antibody; REQUEST TEST: Single_fiber_EMG.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_receptor_antibodies: Present (elevated); Single_fiber_EMG: Not performed.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. Based on your classic presentation of fluctuating weakness that worsens with activity and improves with rest, combined with double vision triggered by looking up or down, the clinical picture is highly specific to this condition. The requested antibody and EMG tests are the definitive next steps to confirm this.
